title: Volume 2 Chapter 1: The Girl Named Kuzunoha Mahiro
content: The first thing that came to mind when I first heard the name Kuzunoha Mahiro was,
"I wonder what kanji she uses for that?
The next time I heard her name, I was informed of her physical measurements and couldn’t help but ask, "Huh?"
And by the third time, I was left speechless, thinking,
"Is our university filled with girls like that?
" After that, whenever she came up in conversation, I would just respond with vague nods.
In other words, Kuzunoha Mahiro was a cute girl with a raccoon-like face, known for her impressive physical features.
She had a refined style reminiscent of a news anchor, yet possessed an H-cup bust.
Rumor had it that she had dated and broken up with three different virgins in a single month, and it was said that ten virgins had matured into men under her influence over the course of a year.
Her infamous reputation rivaled that of my girlfriend, Tendou Tsukasa, and while the backlash from other girls was intense, she had never been without a boyfriend for long.
Even those aware of her reputation still thought,
[img]https://i.imgur.com/FF1ZQKT.jpeg
"I’m different,
" and continued to pursue her.
In short, Kuzunoha seemed like an invincible presence, indifferent to her bad reputation.
That said, I was engaged to Tsukasa this rainy season and had been devoted to her.
By summer vacation, we had officially become a couple, and I lost my virginity (it was amazing).
So, Kuzunoha Mahiro was nothing more than a classmate who was a friend of my girlfriend, and I had no intention of getting involved with her.
That was my plan, at least.
"Hey, Iori-kun, are you still dating Tsukasa-chan?"
"Uh, yeah, I am."
Kuzunoha, with her strong accent that contributed to the backlash from girls, leaned in closer than necessary during the lecture and narrowed her large eyes into a playful smile.
I was forced into an awkward position to avoid her ample assets.
I had a bad feeling about this.
Specifically, it was the same feeling I got when Tsukasa was plotting something I couldn’t resist.
A wind was definitely blowing in a direction unfavorable to me.
"I see, that’s a bit disappointing, huh?"
If a friend is doing well with their boyfriend, isn’t it normal to congratulate them?
I swallowed the words that might have turned into a snake in the grass and simply prayed to the heavens that this storm would pass quickly.
"Then how about we secretly date too?"
Of course, just as I feared, that little prayer was shattered.
"—Mahiro, could you stop bothering Iori-kun?"
On a September afternoon, still warm from the lingering summer heat, Tsukasa sharply addressed Kuzunoha, who was sitting across from her at a shaded terrace table.
However, her voice and expression lacked any real hostility, making me think that their friendship was genuine and not just a mutual benefit for two bad girls.
"Eh, I’m not doing anything like that!"
In response to Tsukasa’s questioning, Kuzunoha maintained her charming smile and replied in a relaxed tone.
Yet, there was something unfathomable about her demeanor.
Well, it didn’t seem like it would escalate into the kind of battlefield I had feared, so I felt a bit relieved.
I had no experience with such situations, and I was almost losing my mind thinking I’d have to tell them not to fight over me...
"You’re the one who invited him to cheat, and you say that?"
"I didn’t mean it like that! Don’t get mad!"
"Then what did you mean...?"
However, with Tsukasa’s undeniable beauty and Kuzunoha’s cute charm, their playful banter drew the attention of those around us.
The sheer attractiveness of their faces was overwhelming, and they probably emitted some kind of photogenic negative ions (just a guess).
If this were a more peaceful conversation, I could have relaxed, but...
"Listen, Iori-kun is a decent person."
"Unlike us?"
"Exactly."
"Ah, it’s funny to hear Tsukasa-chan say that."
"Not something to laugh about—this isn’t a joke."
As Tsukasa corrected herself with a bitter expression, almost slipping into her accent, Kuzunoha smiled with a
"Nihi
" expression.
"Hey, why did you correct yourself just now? Come on, Tsukasa-chan?"
"Well, it doesn’t matter, does it?"
Kuzunoha is supposedly from Nagasaki, but her accent shares many similarities with Fukuoka, and perhaps due to her laid-back way of speaking, it stuck in my ears and pulled me in...
"Why don’t you talk like that when it’s just the two of us, Tsukasa-chan?"
"Well, it’s not just the two of us now, so it’s not weird to act differently."
And with that, Tsukasa was getting drawn into the conversation, slightly losing her grip on the situation.
Hmm, this laid-back demeanor is surprisingly formidable.
"But Iori-kun isn’t bothered, right?"
"Actually, I called Tsukasa-san here because I was bothered. Also, could you stop casually calling me by my name?"
"Eh, but I call Tsukasa-chan by her name, so don’t you like it when I call you Iori-kun?"
Oh, that person is my (important) girlfriend, so it’s fine.
Well, she’s my girlfriend.
It’s not that I dislike my name, but I don’t like being called by my name by someone I don’t know well.
That said, to be honest, I’ve gotten used to Tsukasa calling me by my name lately, so it doesn’t bother me as much anymore.
I still want to put my foot down about those who jokingly call me
"Iorin,
" and I’d like to make it clear about Kuzunoha calling me by my name.
"Then if you got to know me better, it’d be fine!"
Hmm, she doesn’t seem interested in listening.
"No way, I’m the only one special to him."
And Tsukasa, who had been a bit more serious during this potential battlefield, looked a bit cute when she boasted about that with just one of my words.
"Eh, then wouldn’t it be better if I became his girlfriend too?"
"‘Not good.’"
What’s going on in her head? I glanced at Tsukasa, who silently shook her head.
Seems like that’s a no...
"What? You two are connecting with your eyes, aren’t you? How hot!"
"Then why do you invite me to cheat...?"
But somehow, I felt a different kind of disconnect from the early days of Tsukasa.
Could it be that attractive women tend to not listen to others...?
"And by the way, Mahiro. Just so you know, Iori-kun is no longer a virgin, so you’re out of luck."
"Was that information really necessary?"
It’s true, but still, I wish she wouldn’t out me like that.
And it’s impressive how she can say it with pride like, "I ate it."
Well, at our age, it’s not unnatural at all, and in fact, considering the length of our relationship, it would be more surprising if it weren’t true.
"Eh? Really?"
"Yeah, why are you doubting me?"
"Because, you know, Tsukasa-chan didn’t like virgins, right?"
"Iori-kun is my first boyfriend, so that’s an exception."
"Why is Kuzunoha so fixated on virgins...?"
Unlike a girl’s virginity, a guy’s virginity isn’t really valued, and I’m not sure why, even though she’s Tsukasa’s friend, she thinks my chastity is still intact.
After all, she invites me to sex as an extension of physical contact, right?
Well, having a beautiful and sexy girlfriend is definitely a welcome element for guys.
Eh, why do I care?
Virgins are such a hassle, right?
They’re really interested in sex but act like they shouldn’t be.
If they peek at my breasts and then look apologetic, it’s just...
"That’s going too far."
"Why?"
I can relate to that, having once been a virgin and now not being one.
It’s a fact, but should I say it’s just a fact?
"Honestly, that seems more like a reason to avoid them."
No, that’s not it!
That’s what I like!
You know, it makes me feel like a goddess!
When they’re thinking about me, wondering if they’ll be liked or not, my heart goes 'kyun' and I just want to do anything for them!
And Iori-kun still feels that way even after dating Tsukasa-chan, so it makes me curious.
"Wow, she’s a crazy girl beyond my expectations..."
What is that twisted maternal instinct... is it maternal instinct?
How does such a laid-back monster come into existence?
Also, the fact that she’s getting a bit too fast-paced is a bit too real.
On top of that, being told I still smell like a virgin (paraphrased) and having no rebuttal is tough.
"This is why I didn’t want to introduce Mahiro too much..."
Next to my shocked self, Tsukasa pressed her fingers to her forehead with a bitter expression.
Does that mean Tsukasa thought I looked like the kind of virgin Kuzunoha would like? That’s painful.
However, it was rare to see her looking so worn out.
Even when I made a series of tactless comments, she didn’t look this bad.
"—Hey, Tsukasa-san. Don’t you think it’s better to choose your friends wisely?"
Sure, everyone has their own social circles, but this is a level that’s a bit hard to cover up.
"I understand where you’re coming from, Iori-kun, but I don’t think I can say that to her."
"Haha—ouch, that hurts."
I agreed that she had a point, and then she slammed her palm on the table.
"And really, other than this, she’s a good girl, really."
"Are you okay? That sounds like the psychology of a domestic violence victim."
"I think I’m okay, but I’m starting to lose confidence..."
"Hehe, you two really get along well."
"If you think that, could you stop trying to tear us apart...?"
"That’s right, Iori-kun is crazy about me, so don’t interfere."
It’s true, but isn’t that a bit loud?
Well, it seems necessary for persuasion, and I won’t stop her from casually holding my hand because it’s cute.
Kuzunoha, who had been watching our hands, let out a slightly wistful sigh.
Well, I don’t really want you two to break up or anything.
When I said secretly, I was joking.
I just thought it’d be nice to share a bit of what Tsukasa-chan has.
"I think that’s a pretty bad joke."
"I don’t have a hobby of sharing my boyfriend."
Doesn’t that have brackets around it like "joke (serious)" or "sharing (taking away)"?
"By the way, Mahiro, didn’t you say you got a boyfriend again before summer? What happened?"
"Well, it didn’t work out after all. Haha."
Kuzunoha, who had been smiling through all the teasing, suddenly looked gloomy.
She took out her smartphone and started flicking through it repeatedly, letting out a big sigh.
"I was just about to hit twenty, so I thought this time would work out..."
"—Oh, that’s unfortunate."
For a moment, I thought, "Oh, is that all?" but I realized my sense of perspective was getting skewed.
Whether it was the number of experiences or boyfriends, twenty is more than enough.
Also, is it a trend for girls like Tsukasa and Kuzunoha to keep records on their smartphones?
Or is it just something I’m unaware of that’s common among girls?
The questions never end.
However, while it might be a serious concern for Kuzunoha, it’s still a hassle for me if she starts bothering me about it...
"Um, can I ask why you broke up with your boyfriend?"
I’ve heard rumors about her dating and breaking up in quick succession, but I didn’t know the specific reasons.
It’s clear she’s a dangerous presence for virgins in many ways, but even now, she doesn’t seem like the type to cheat.
Well, she did invite me, but Kuzunoha is currently single.
Ah, I’m not planning to break up with Tsukasa-san, and I definitely have no intention of dating Kuzunoha, so I’m not saying you should talk about it.
I’m not sure if it’s appropriate for me to stick my neck out, but at the same time, she is Tsukasa’s friend.
Both of them have strong assumptions, so maybe I could offer some advice from a guy’s perspective—could that be a luxury I’m allowed now that I have a girlfriend?
Am I being conceited?
While I felt my insides being pierced by the blade of self-consciousness, I thought, well, if there’s something I can do...
"Well, you know, a guy’s opinion might be helpful."
If that leads to her getting along better with someone else, that’d be great!
"Thanks, Iori-kun... I told Tsukasa-chan, but is it okay if I talk to you?"
"Is that okay, Tsukasa-san?"
"Yeah, that’s fine."
When I glanced at Tsukasa, she looked like she wanted to say something but eventually nodded slightly.
What’s going on? It’s rare for her to seem indecisive, but is there something surprising waiting for me?
I seem to fall in love easily, and as I said earlier, when I get close to a virgin, I can’t help but get curious.
So, I confess and ask them out.
"Uh-huh."
Well, I had a feeling she would be the type to go for it, so it wasn’t surprising at all.
Especially with the recent trend of confused virgins thinking they need to be approached by girls (from personal experience).
So, I let them do whatever they want, and I adjust all the plans for dates and make lunchboxes.
Oh, I want to be a good wife, so I’m good at housework, and I don’t mind being devoted.
...Things are starting to take a turn for the worse, aren’t they?
It was cute when she mentioned wanting to be a wife, but then Tsukasa pinched the back of my hand.
Is she a psychic?
I wish I could convey that Tsukasa is cuter, but...
"Hey, are you really listening?"
"I’m listening, I’m listening."
Then that’s good... but then, at first, my boyfriend would call me a goddess or an angel, but as we dated, he became distant!
He started saying I was lewd, and even during sex, he’d say horrible things!
He’d start looking at other girls too!
Isn’t that awful!?
It’s not like I can just break up, right!?
I see?
"—Tsukasa-san, this is a bit hard to say..."
"Well, it’s hard to say that Mahiro has no part in this..."
"Eh, why!? Why would you say something like that to a friend!? Tsukasa-chan, that’s cruel! Iori-kun, you’re cold too!"
I felt relieved to have Tsukasa’s agreement, but it seemed Kuzunoha was not satisfied with that response.
She sounded betrayed, but isn’t it pretty harsh to act like a convenient girl and then pull the rug out from under someone once they start getting interested?
Sure, the boyfriend should exercise self-control, but it’s not surprising that a virgin would get carried away if a beauty like her fawned over him.
"Well, I think it’s not good to spoil a virgin who doesn’t know how to interact with girls."
Is that too much of a guy’s perspective? But logically, that seems like it could be the cause.
If Tsukasa had been that kind of character, it’s possible I could have turned into a clingy monster boyfriend digging into the past by now.
"Because they’re cute! It’s only natural to want to spoil them!"
"Well... and while I think the boyfriend’s change is a problem, did you ever talk about it with him?"
"No? Because he stopped liking me, so I didn’t want to do that, and I didn’t like him either."
When I looked at Tsukasa, she again shook her head silently.
Alright, this isn’t good!
"I see—well, I hope you meet a good person someday, then."
"Eh!? Why are you suddenly losing interest!?"
"Well, because Kuzunoha, you’re not really interested in listening to others..."
"At times like this, you should say, 'You’re not at fault, that’s right!'"
"Why do I have to say something I don’t mean?"
"The boys who listen to my problems usually say that!"
That’s probably because they had ulterior motives.
Well, you see, now we understand the difference in values between me and Kuzunoha, right?
For now, let’s stop doing something pointless and crazy like hitting on a friend’s boyfriend.
"—Hey, Tsukasa-chan, is Iori-kun always this harsh? I’ve never met someone who would say I’m crazy to my face!"
"Iori-kun’s way of speaking is harsh, but I think the content is valid."
"Ugh... then I won’t say I want to date you, so can you at least be friends with me, Iori-kun?"
What does "then" mean? And doesn’t that have the nuance of "let’s start as friends"?
"Tsukasa-san, can I trust this?"
Well—hey Mahiro, just so you know, Iori-kun is completely devoid of blood and tears in situations like this.
If you have any strange expectations, you’ll end up with wounds that never heal.
"Wait, my evaluation is terrible."
"Tsukasa-chan, what do you like about that kind of person?"
Stop asking me with a serious face. I might cry.
"Pretty much everything, is that bad?"
And can you stop with the emotional rollercoaster of dropping and lifting me?
I wish you’d say it when I could be more genuinely happy.
"Eh, you can say that? I’m so jealous... I was wondering what’s different since Tsukasa-chan is being treated so well."
What Kuzunoha said then felt like it was genuinely from her heart.
Well, everyone has their own circumstances. Whether I can empathize or not is a different story.
"I’m sorry, Iori-kun, Tsukasa-chan. But I really want to be friends."
Since I have a girlfriend in Tsukasa, I don’t want to get too involved in other girls’ situations.
I won’t get too involved, but if Tsukasa isn’t cutting ties, then being friends is... well...
"I’m fine with it. Mahiro has helped me before."
"Oh, that persistent virgin? You didn’t have to be that grateful for that."
But looking back on those memories, I didn’t really want to know...
"—Well, since she’s Tsukasa-san’s friend, I guess I can manage to be friends... yeah... well... yeah..."
"Iori-kun, if you’re struggling that much, maybe you should just decline? You don’t have to feel obligated to me."
"No, it’s fine... yeah, it’s fine, yeah, it’s good."
"Really? I’m glad. If you said you didn’t want to be friends, that would be tough."
That’s a pretty harsh way to put it...
It’s really hard to decline. If this is all calculated, isn’t she tougher than Tsukasa?
Well, but everything is an experience, and the boundary between acquaintances and friends is ambiguous unless you completely ignore it.
"Then, Iori-kun, let’s shake hands?"
"Oh, yeah, that’s fine."
As I shook Kuzunoha’s outstretched hand, I felt a softness different from Tsukasa’s.
And then, as she silently squeezed my hand, I suddenly remembered something.
"Hey, Iori-kun. Can we talk just the two of us in a quiet place later?"
"No way!"
"Mahiro?"
As expected, those words carried an unpleasant stickiness, and without any shame, I pulled my hand away.
Thus, Tsukasa and I jointly declared a one-week ban on Kuzunoha’s approach to me.
